featured_reviews.name: NAFIS AHMED
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ramadan evenings at Minara Masjid on Mohammed Ali Road are truly magical....the entire stretch from Sulaiman Usman Mithaiwala to Chinese n Grill comes alive with vibrant lights, mouth-watering aromas, and an unbeatable festive atmosphere. It’s not just a food destination, it’s an experience that captures the true spirit of Ramadan in Mumbai..
The food stalls offer an incredible variety — from juicy seekh kebabs of Bade Miyan...Badami Hyderabadi haleem to rich Mutton Nalli Nihari of Chinese n Grill, the tasty creamy Kesar Phirni and refreshing Milk kesar juice of Noorani Milk Centre...Every dish feels authentic, freshly prepared, and full of flavor. The smoky grills and sizzling tavas add to the charm, making it impossible to walk past without stopping.
Despite the heavy crowd, the energy  the vibes is positive and joyful. Families, friends, and food lovers gather together, creating a beautiful sense of community. If you want to experience Mumbai’s Ramadan food culture at its best, Mohammed Ali Road near Minara Masjid is an absolute must-visit!!

featured_reviews.name: Buddy Caprice
featured_reviews.review_text: A very popular place during Ramadan to try the special dishes that are generally not available throughout the year! Hygiene is a big issue, especially during weekends. However there are some really great options to try when here. The Dal Khichda from Keshodwala Food corner along with their Galouti kebabs, Sweets from ZamZam Sweets and Malpua Rabdi from Tawakkal Sweets and Suleman Usman Bakery are a must try. For hard core non vegetarians, please try the Batair Tandoori (Quail) from Mashallah Restaurant right in the middle of the street. Another must try is the Mutton Haleem from a smaller but crowded food stall a little ahead of Mashallah Restaurant called the Hyderabadi Badami Haleem stall. Other options available that will not upset your stomach are the baida rotis, bheja fry, liver fry, chaaps, seekh kebabs, etc. but those are available on almost all food stalls laid out there and elsewhere in Mumbai. Another special item to try is the Sandal, a sweet dish made of khoya/maava. The firni also is especially available during these weeks. Halva paratha are also available but are not recommended from here due to hygiene issues. The costs are really nominal like ₹50 for Dal Khichda, ₹150 for Haleem, ₹50 for 3-4 pieces of Galouti Kebabs, and so on. The most expensive dish was the Batair Tandoori at Mashallah. Lot of other takeaways too from clothes, toys, Islamic materials, shoes, etc. Also there are Ittr and Perfume shops everywhere. A must not miss is the "Mohabbat wala Sharbat", a cool and refreshing Watermelon-Rose Milk-Sabza based drink that is a commonly spotted item everywhere. Travelling to this lane could be quite tedious and no taxis risk going into this zone during Ramadan, so recommend to take your own vehicles since even Ola/Uber rides cancel due to frustrating traffic. No taxis are ready to take you back to even 2-3 stations away and drop you. It's a fun place for every food lover and explorer at once during this season, only if you are ok with management amongst chaos! 😁

featured_reviews.review_text:
Food Street, Mumbai – A Taste of Bombay’s Best

Excellent and tasty food is served here at Food Street, Mumbai, a popular destination for anyone who loves authentic Bombay flavors. This place brings together the city’s most famous street foods under one roof, offering a mix of taste, aroma, and tradition that Mumbai is known for. From the spicy kick of vada pav and the buttery goodness of pav bhaji to the tangy bhel puri and crispy sev puri, every dish reflects the city’s rich food culture.

The chefs here prepare each item with care, using fresh ingredients and maintaining the original Bombay taste that food lovers crave. Whether you prefer light snacks or filling meals, there’s something for everyone. The lively atmosphere, quick service, and friendly staff make dining here an enjoyable experience.

Food Street isn’t just a place to eat—it’s a celebration of Mumbai’s vibrant street food heritage. Locals come here to relive nostalgic flavors, while visitors get a true introduction to the city’s culinary charm. If you’re in Mumbai and looking for delicious, authentic, and affordable food, Food Street is the perfect stop to satisfy your hunger and enjoy Bombay’s famous taste in every bite.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this eatery on Mohamadalli Road during the Holy Month of Ramadan. It's just opposite Minara Masjid.

Obviously it was jam packed. They have seating outside on the road (maybe only in the month of ramadan... good to avoid, unless you are in a hurry) and AC inside (much better).

We tried their signature Chicken Tandoori Platter (for around Rs.1550 you can have a little of everything, quite huge in size with around 6-7 items and around 4 pieces each and good for around 4 big eaters), and it was good. Unfortunately and maybe due to the crowd, they end up burning / overcooking some of the items and it gets quite tough to bite.

Service was fast and waiters are very pleasant and smiling. They are patient enough to explain you the dishes.

Sadly even in the AC section we were getting an odd smell... If you don't worry about the ambience, you will enjoy your meal.

Rates are maybe steep, but worth the servings.

We tried a good variety of starters including pani puri, dahi batata puri, masala khichiya papad, Harabhara kabab, kachori chaat and dahi bhalla. The dahi batata puri clearly stood out. The balance of sweet, tangy, and spicy flavors was spot on and easily the highlight of the starters.

featured_reviews.name: Jatin Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Atria Mall is where one finds loads of options to choose from in terms of having their meal and it is home to Bombay Street Co. - paradise for vegetarians. Located at Level 0 the place gives you an experience of a chaat bazaar in a sophisticated environment. And that's where I believe Bombay Street Co. scores against other restaurants. Providing the best of street food in a hygienic environment. Now since the restaurant is a pure veg restaurant, it shall have its own flipside of attracting large groups and families and it tends to get a little noisy. But if one is fine with it, believe it's the place to head to.

Talking about what all I tried here -

We called for couple of starters - Youger Poppers and Veg Tandoori Platter. Of the two, I would personally recommend all to try the Younger Poppers, quite different from the jalapeno cheese poppers. In this it's a combination of capsicum, cheese crushed with papadam. Tandoori Platter is a serving of kebabs - Tandoori Aloo, Paneer Tikka, Tandoori Mushrooms and Tandoori Baby Corn. A bit of work needed specially for the mushrooms and baby corn, they weren't grilled enough. Aloo was nice and so was paneer.

Along with food, we ordered for couple of drinks - Mint Mojito and Spice Guava Chilli. Both drinks quite basic but refreshing, solves the purpose. Some work can be done towards the presentation of drinks perhaps. Moving to the mains, as mentioned earlier the place offers scrumptious street food in a good ambience. So was excited to try the Pizza Dosa straight from Anna Ki Galli. Superb fusion of 2 dishes. Believe this and Gini dosa as usual would be the regular favorites of all at this restaurant. Something one should not miss.

Last but not the least, tried couple of desserts - Gulab Jamun with Vanilla and Jalebi with Rabdi. Both were recommending and trying basis preference taste and choice. Mind you, one gets a plate full of Jalebi so you may need a few to share the plate. But tastes heavenly, so does the combination of gulab jamun with Vanilla Ice-cream scoop.

All-in-all a paradise for pure veg food eaters who prefer going to places which don't serve non veg food. And ofcourse street food with a great combo of taste and hygiene. Do pay a visit when possible.

🔹️Chopper Rice - An amazing Chinese main course of fried rice, noodles, manchurian balls and exotic veggies gravies ... All in one plate was superb in presentation, taste as well as quantity.
🔹️ Kesar Jalebi - Hot and crispy Jalebis topped with dryfruits was succulent and luscious.

So I happen to drop by this restaurant and the name says it all "Bombay Street Co" and it seems that they love Mumbai as much as we do. It's a vegetarian restaurant. featured_reviews.name: Travelling Doctor
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sun & Moon: A Hidden Gem for Authentic Korean Comfort

If you’re craving a taste of Seoul that feels truly homemade, Sun & Moon is a fantastic find. It avoids the polished, corporate feel of many modern franchises, opting instead for a cozy, down-to-earth vibe that focuses entirely on the plate.

The Food: Bold, Authentic, and Filling
The menu is a love letter to Korean street food and classic staples. Here were the highlights of my meal:
Korean Corn Dog: Hands down, one of the best I’ve had. It had that perfect golden crunch on the outside and was incredibly satisfying. A must-order if you're a fan of this snack.
Tteokbokki: If you like a bit of a kick, this is for you. The sauce was spicy yet deeply savoury, with the rice cakes cooked to a perfect chewy consistency. It’s the kind of heat that keeps you coming back for more.
Bibimbap: This was a very hearty portion. While the flavor profile was a little on the bland side compared to the spicy tteokbokki, it was packed with a generous variety of fresh, crisp vegetables. The star here was the amazing sticky rice, which pulled the whole dish together. It’s a great, filling option if you want something wholesome.

Atmosphere and Service
The restaurant itself is clearly a local favorite that has been around for a while. To be honest, the place is showing its age—the interior feels a bit dated and "lived-in." However, what it lacks in modern decor, it more than makes up for with soul and hospitality.
The service was amazing; the staff were attentive, welcoming, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal. There is also a small section where you can buy souvenirs, though the selection is a bit limited. It’s a nice touch if you want to pick up a small trinket or a Korean snack to go, but don't expect a full gift shop experience.

Final Thoughts
Sun & Moon is perfect for those who prioritize authentic flavor and warm service over a fancy interior. It’s honest, delicious Korean comfort food that leaves you full and happy. I’ll definitely be back for that corn dog!

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

featured_reviews.name: Amiit k Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing meal at Mao Family Restaurant–Best family Restaurant Kalbadevi-Best North Indian,Mughlai,Chinese,Arabian,Seafood Restaurant Kalbadevi! 😍

The Paneer Schezwan Khepsa Rice was packed with flavor, perfectly spicy, and loaded with delicious paneer pieces. The Manchurian Chatpata was crispy, tangy, and a perfect starter. The highlight was definitely the Hungama Khepsa Rice — huge portion size, rich taste, and enough to satisfy the whole group. Every bite was flavorful and satisfying.

Great food quality, generous portions, and excellent value for money. A must-visit place for Khepsa lovers in Mumbai! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.name: Samruddhi Hambire
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Mao Family Restaurant for lunch and tried the Hungama Kepsa (half) — good portion size and flavorful, definitely worth it. The Chicken Tandoori was outstanding; juicy, well-marinated, and something I would surely recommend to any non-vegetarian.However, the vegetarian menu was a huge disappointment. The Paneer Kepsa tasted more like a Chinese-style gravy than authentic Kepsa, and the Paneer Crispy was neither crispy nor made from real paneer — it was clearly synthetic. At ₹265, the quantity and quality of paneer were unacceptable.In short, this place is a delight for non-vegetarians but a nightmare for vegetarians.

featured_reviews.review_text: The food quality at Mao Restaurant is very poor. The rice is often undercooked and completely tasteless. The overall quality of the food is extremely disappointing. featured_reviews.name: bhavika jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mao Restaurant and had an incredible dining experience! I ordered the Chicken Noorani Kabab and Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa, and I must say, the kababs were absolutely delicious. They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

featured_reviews.name: Himanshu Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Subject: Complaint Regarding Food Quality (Delivery Order)

Respected Sir/Madam,

I recently ordered food from your restaurant through a delivery service. I ordered a half plate of Chilly Kepsa, but my experience was very disappointing.

The boiled egg in the dish had a very bad smell, which made the food inedible. This clearly indicates that the food was not fresh and raises serious concerns about hygiene and quality.

I request you to please look into this matter seriously and ensure that proper quality checks are done before sending food for delivery.

I hope you will take necessary action so that such issues do not happen again.

Thank you.

Yours sincerely,
Himanshu Gupta

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Akhade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would never give the review or recommend this place to any one, On 17/04/2026, my friends and I visited the restaurant for dinner. After finishing our meal, we stepped outside and were waiting for a cab when one of my friends suddenly collapsed due to low blood pressure and fainted right outside your restaurant.

In that moment of urgency, I approached your staff requesting a small amount of sugar to help revive her. However, I was shocked by their response—they bluntly said they do not keep sugar. What was even more surprising was that at the same time, sugar was clearly available in the mukhwas kept there.

It was a matter of basic human kindness, and such a small help could have made a big difference in that situation. Unfortunately, the staff showed complete lack of empathy and humanity.

This is particularly disappointing because Kalbadevi has always been a place we frequently visit for lunch and dinner. Experiencing such insensitive behavior from your team was unexpected and unacceptable.

I do have a video of the incident, I will upload it soon. I will Raise a complaint too.

featured_reviews.name: Brijesh Trivedi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this restaurant on my wife's birthday, drawn in by its great ambience and inviting atmosphere. The decor and setting were well thought out, making for an enjoyable dining environment.

We ordered a couple of starters, sushi, and a main dish. While the starters were flavorful, the quantity did not justify the price, leaving us feeling that the portions could have been more generous. The real disappointment came when we discovered a long hair in our sushi. This instantly raised concerns about the quality and hygiene of the food.

When we pointed this out to the staff, they handled the situation politely and professionally, taking the dish away and offering us a replacement. While this was appreciated, the incident had already dampened our experience, and we chose to simply request the bill instead.

Surprisingly, the bill still included charges for the sushi as well as service charges. Upon bringing this to their attention, the staff quickly removed those charges. However, they should not have been added in the first place, given the situation.

One positive takeaway was the politeness and courteousness of the staff, who handled the issue without hesitation. Despite this, the combination of portion concerns and an unfortunate hygiene lapse made this an experience we wouldn't eagerly return for.
